title: Pizza Dough
subtitle: Classic Neapolitan pizza dough with a long, cold ferment
excerpt: A simple, high-hydration Neapolitan pizza dough that develops flavour through a slow, cold fermentation. Stretch it thin, top it simply, and bake at the highest heat your oven will reach.

recipe.sourceNotes: Neapolitan pizza is the original form of pizza, originating in the city of Naples in the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. The first documented reference to pizza in Naples dates to 997 CE, though the dish as it is now known developed in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana (AVPN), established in 1984, sets strict standards for traditional Neapolitan pizza: the dough must use Tipo 00 flour or a blend with Tipo 0, natural yeast (or a small amount of commercial yeast), water, sea salt, and nothing else. The dough must ferment for at least 8 hours at room temperature. The pizza must be baked in a wood-fired oven at 430 to 480 C for 60 to 90 seconds. Home ovens cannot reach this temperature, but a very hot domestic oven (250 C or higher) with a preheated baking stone or steel produces a good result with a longer baking time. The characteristic char spots on a good Neapolitan pizza are the cornicione, the raised edge, darkening in the intense heat.

recipeTools.notes: A baking stone or thick baking tray, preheated for at least 30 minutes in the oven.

content.text: Stretch the dough by hand rather than rolling with a pin: a rolling pin pushes out the air bubbles that give the crust its open, chewy texture. Working from the centre and rotating the dough, stretch it gradually over your knuckles. The dough should be almost translucent at the centre. Preheat the oven to its highest temperature (250 C or above) with the baking stone or tray inside for at least 30 to 45 minutes: a cold stone will produce a soggy base.

items.preparation: Tipo 00 if available, or strong bread flour

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt. Add 325 ml of cool water and the olive oil. Mix to a shaggy dough, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be tacky but not sticky.

Divide into 4 equal balls (about 210 g each). Place each on an oiled surface, cover tightly, and refrigerate for 1 to 3 days. The long cold fermentation develops flavour. Remove from the fridge 2 hours before using.

Heat the oven to its highest setting (at least 250 C) with the baking stone inside for 30 to 45 minutes. Stretch each dough ball to a 30 cm round. Top with tomato sauce and cheese. Slide onto the stone and bake for 8 to 12 minutes until the base is crisp and the edges are lightly charred.
